author: lasusu
description:
Detects cloud and IAM discovery from a session whose STS session name is an EC2 instance ID. This distinguishes
instance-profile activity from ordinary assumed roles used by Terraform, service integrations, or administrators.
false_positives: Approved inventory or compliance software running under an EC2 instance profile.
name: AWS EC2 Instance Unusual Cloud Enumeration Activity
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the instance-profile session ARN, discovery APIs, source IP, and any preceding SSM activity. The STS session name must be an EC2 instance ID, so an ordinary administrator or Terraform assumed role does not match.

Verify that the instance and role normally perform inventory work. Treat failed cross-service enumeration from an unexpected instance as a possible indication of instance-role credential compromise.

### False positive analysis

Do not exclude all EC2 instance roles. Scope any exception to a known inventory role and document the APIs it is permitted to use.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and aws.cloudtrail.user_identity.type: "AssumedRole"
  and user.id: *i-*
  and event.action: ("ListBuckets" or "GetAccountSummary" or "ListRoles" or "ListUsers" or "GetAccountAuthorizationDetails")

author: lasusu
description:
Detects modification of an EC2 Security Group allowing unrestricted inbound SSH access (port 22) from the public
Internet (0.0.0.0/0). Exposing management port 22 publicly exposes compute infrastructure to brute-force attacks,
unauthorized SSH access, and initial access compromises.
false_positives: An approved bastion host or break-glass maintenance window that intentionally exposes SSH to the Internet for a short period.
name: AWS EC2 Security Group Opened SSH Port 22 to the Internet
note:
## Triage and analysis

Confirm the security group, CIDR, protocol, port range, actor, and affected workload. This rule detects the successful configuration change; it does not prove that an SSH login occurred.

If the exposure is unapproved, revoke the ingress rule, identify instances using the group, and review VPC Flow Logs and host authentication logs for follow-on access.

### False positive analysis

Public SSH can be temporarily approved for a bastion or recovery operation. Prefer a time-bounded exception tied to one security group rather than an identity-wide exception.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail" 
  and event.provider: "ec2.amazonaws.com" 
  and event.action: "AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress" 
  and event.outcome: "success" 
  and (
    (
      aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.fromPort: 22
      and aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.cidrIp: ("0.0.0.0/0" or "::/0")
    )
    or (
      aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.ipPermissions.items.fromPort: 22
      and aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.ipPermissions.items.ipRanges.items.cidrIp: ("0.0.0.0/0" or "::/0")
    )
  )

author: lasusu
description: Detects modifications or code overwrites to existing AWS Lambda functions via the UpdateFunctionCode API. Adversaries may inject malicious code into existing serverless functions to establish persistent access, backdoor serverless workflows, or execute unauthorized code within the cloud environment.
false_positives: Approved CI/CD deployments, rollback operations, and emergency hotfixes that update Lambda code.
name: AWS Lambda Function Code Modification or Overwrite
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the function name, code source fields, actor, source IP, user agent, and deployment context. A successful UpdateFunctionCode confirms a code change, not malicious code or execution.

Validate the change against the release pipeline, source repository, artifact hash, and change ticket. If unapproved, disable or roll back the function using the incident process and review its execution role, triggers, and recent invocations.

### False positive analysis

Frequent Lambda deployments are expected in mature environments. Prefer exceptions for a specific CI/CD role and repository workflow; do not suppress updates from all deployment identities.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail" 
  and event.provider: "lambda.amazonaws.com" 
  and event.action: ("UpdateFunctionCode20150331v2" or "UpdateFunctionCode") 
  and event.outcome: "success"

author: lasusu
description: Detects denied attempts to retrieve the userData attribute of an EC2 instance through DescribeInstanceAttribute.
false_positives: Expected debugging or deployment automation using a role that has not yet received DescribeInstanceAttribute permission.
name: Suspended or Denied EC2 User Data Enumeration Attempts
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the actor, target instance ID, source IP, and error code. This rule covers denied discovery attempts; a successful user-data retrieval is covered by a separate detection policy because it represents confirmed access.

Verify whether the instance ID exists and whether the role should inspect user data. Multiple failures against unrelated instances should be investigated as reconnaissance.

### False positive analysis

Infrastructure automation may fail during a rollout because of delayed IAM propagation. Validate the deployment identity and ticket before creating an exception.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail" 
  and event.provider: "ec2.amazonaws.com" 
  and event.action: "DescribeInstanceAttribute" 
  and event.outcome: "failure" 
  and aws.cloudtrail.error_code: "Client.UnauthorizedOperation"
  and aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.attribute: "userData"

author: lasusu
description:
Detects denied attempts to launch high-compute GPU EC2 instances. This rule targets the combination of an unusual instance
family and a permission or quota failure, which is consistent with early resource-hijacking attempts.
false_positives: Approved capacity testing, quota validation, or GPU deployment attempts that are expected to fail before the quota or IAM policy is granted.
name: Denied EC2 High-Compute GPU Instance Launch
note:
## Triage and analysis

Confirm the requested instance family, error code, actor, source IP, and related Service Quotas requests. The rule intentionally requires both a GPU family and a denied or quota-limited launch; a generic denied RunInstances request does not match.

Determine whether the actor was approved to provision GPU capacity. Investigate repeated attempts, new source locations, and follow-on IAM policy changes as possible resource hijacking.

### False positive analysis

Engineering teams can trigger this during capacity planning. Validate a ticket or an allow-listed deployment role before suppressing a specific role or region.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and event.provider: "ec2.amazonaws.com"
  and event.action: "RunInstances"
  and event.outcome: "failure"
  and aws.cloudtrail.error_code: ("Client.UnauthorizedOperation" or "VcpuLimitExceeded")
  and aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.instanceType: (p2.* or p3.* or p4.* or p5.* or g3.* or g4.* or g5.* or g6.*)

author: lasusu
name: AWS EC2 Instance User Data Modified
description: Detects a successful EC2 instance user-data change. User data can execute commands on boot and may be used to establish execution or persistence on an existing instance.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and event.provider: "ec2.amazonaws.com"
  and event.action: "ModifyInstanceAttribute"
  and event.outcome: "success"
  and aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.userData: *
false_positives: Approved instance bootstrap, image maintenance, or configuration automation can update user data. Validate the target instance and change request.
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the actor, source IP, user agent, request parameters, and adjacent CloudTrail activity. Confirm that the activity is expected for the responsible workload before creating a narrowly scoped exception.

author: lasusu
name: AWS SageMaker Notebook Lifecycle Configuration Changed
description: Detects creation of a SageMaker notebook lifecycle configuration or attachment of one to a notebook instance. Lifecycle scripts execute on the notebook and can be used for persistence or code execution.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and event.provider: "sagemaker.amazonaws.com"
  and event.action: ("CreateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig" or "UpdateNotebookInstance")
  and event.outcome: "success"
false_positives: Approved data-science platform automation may create or attach lifecycle configurations. Exclude dedicated SageMaker deployment roles only after validation.
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the actor, source IP, user agent, request parameters, and adjacent CloudTrail activity. Confirm that the activity is expected for the responsible workload before creating a narrowly scoped exception.

author: lasusu
name: AWS EC2 AMI Deregistered
description: Detects successful deregistration of an EC2 Amazon Machine Image. Removing an AMI can disrupt recovery, deployments, or availability.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and event.provider: "ec2.amazonaws.com"
  and event.action: "DeregisterImage"
  and event.outcome: "success"
false_positives: Approved AMI retirement or image-pipeline cleanup may deregister images. Validate the owner and asset lifecycle before responding.
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the actor, source IP, user agent, request parameters, and adjacent CloudTrail activity. Confirm that the activity is expected for the responsible workload before creating a narrowly scoped exception.

author: lasusu
name: AWS Secrets Manager High-Volume Secret Retrieval
description: Detects five successful secret-value retrievals by one identity and client in the rule interval. The threshold covers the Stratus single-secret and batch-retrieval scenarios while avoiding alerts for one or two routine reads.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and event.provider: "secretsmanager.amazonaws.com"
  and event.action: ("GetSecretValue" or "BatchGetSecretValue")
  and event.outcome: "success"
false_positives: Application startup, deployment, or secret rotation automation may retrieve several secrets. Exclude only approved workload identities after validation.
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the actor, source IP, user agent, request parameters, and adjacent CloudTrail activity. Confirm that the activity is expected for the responsible workload before creating a narrowly scoped exception.

author: lasusu
description: Detects one caller creating an IAM user and then creating a long-term access key within ten minutes. Creating a user followed by an access key is a high-risk persistence sequence; a rename is optional and must not be required for detection.
false_positives: Approved break-glass or IAM provisioning workflows can create a user and access key. Restrict exceptions to the dedicated provisioning role and ticketed workflow.
name: AWS IAM User Backdoor Creation Sequence
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the caller, source IP, created user, target of CreateAccessKey, and surrounding IAM activity. The rule detects a risky provisioning sequence; it does not itself prove that the new key was used maliciously.

### False positive analysis

Approved break-glass or IAM provisioning workflows can create a user and access key. Restrict exceptions to the dedicated provisioning role and ticketed workflow.
query:
sequence by aws.cloudtrail.user_identity.arn with maxspan=10m
  [any where data_stream.dataset == "aws.cloudtrail"
    and event.provider == "iam.amazonaws.com"
    and event.action == "CreateUser"
    and event.outcome == "success"]
  [any where data_stream.dataset == "aws.cloudtrail"
    and event.provider == "iam.amazonaws.com"
    and event.action == "CreateAccessKey"
    and event.outcome == "success"]

author: lasusu
description: Detects remote shell execution submitted through AWS Systems Manager SendCommand using the AWS-managed RunShellScript document. A successful request is execution-capable, but should be triaged against the responsible automation and maintenance context.
false_positives: Approved patching, software deployment, or incident-response automation using AWS-RunShellScript.
name: AWS SSM RunShellScript Command Execution
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the actor, source IP, SSM document name, target instance IDs, and command output. CloudTrail confirms command submission, but not command completion or decrypted parameters.

### False positive analysis

Patching and deployment systems can use AWS-RunShellScript. Validate the automation identity, maintenance window, document name, and target tags before adding a narrow exception.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and event.provider: "ssm.amazonaws.com"
  and event.action: "SendCommand"
  and event.outcome: "success"
  and aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.documentName: "AWS-RunShellScript"

author: lasusu
description: Detects a successful AWS Systems Manager Session Manager session started against an EC2 instance. A session provides interactive remote access and should be reviewed when the initiating identity, source, target, or maintenance context is unexpected.
false_positives: Approved operations, incident response, or engineering support sessions through Session Manager.
name: AWS SSM Session Manager Session Started
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the initiating identity, source IP, target instance ID, session ID, and adjacent IAM or SSM activity. CloudTrail confirms an interactive SSM session; investigate the instance and Session Manager logs to determine commands executed during it.

### False positive analysis

Session Manager is a legitimate administration channel. Keep exceptions scoped to a dedicated support or automation identity and documented maintenance workflow; do not suppress all StartSession activity.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and event.provider: "ssm.amazonaws.com"
  and event.action: "StartSession"
  and event.outcome: "success"

author: lasusu
description: Detects repeated batch retrieval of AWS Systems Manager SecureString parameters with decryption enabled. The rule distinguishes a burst of GetParameters calls from an individual GetParameter read, which is more commonly used by application configuration workflows.
false_positives: Approved deployment, secret-rotation, or configuration automation retrieving SecureString parameters in batches.
name: AWS SSM Bulk SecureString Parameter Retrieval with Decryption
note:
## Triage and analysis

Review the calling identity, source IP, user agent, requested parameter names, KMS key policy, and adjacent Secrets Manager or IAM activity. The alert means at least five decrypted batch parameter retrievals were requested within the 30-minute lookback; it does not expose decrypted values.

### False positive analysis

Approved deployment and configuration systems can retrieve several SecureStrings. Validate the automation identity, target parameter path, and change context. Scope any exception to a named workload identity and expected parameter prefix rather than suppressing all SSM retrieval.
query:
data_stream.dataset: "aws.cloudtrail"
  and event.provider: "ssm.amazonaws.com"
  and event.action: "GetParameters"
  and event.outcome: "success"
  and aws.cloudtrail.flattened.request_parameters.withDecryption: true
